title: Ghost Lows: an open benchmark for real-time CGM low-glucose alarms under sensor faults
description: Continuous glucose monitors (CGMs) can report false lows, often when the wearer lies on the sensor (pressure-induced sensor attenuation, PISA, or compression lows), and real-time low-glucose alarms then fire without a true low. Ghost Lows is an open benchmark that scores such alarms on lows caught, false alarms per day and minutes of warning under a mixed sensor-fault suite (compression, dropout, stale readings, drift, spikes), with a controlled ablation of what insulin and carbohydrate context adds. In 30 virtual patients (UVA/Padova simulator) with a compression low every night, compression caused 0.32 (95% CI 0.30–0.35) of a trend alarm's 1.53 (1.33–1.73) false alarms per day; insulin and carbohydrate context never cut compression false alarms by the pre-registered 25%, and published compression detectors reduced them only by missing severe lows (post hoc). Includes the benchmark (ghostlows-bench v1), its results, checks on two public CGM datasets, a Python package and an upload report that runs in the browser. Research software; not a medical device.
notes: Co-authors with equal contribution: Pranav Reddy and Cohen Ferrari. Independent project by UCSB students; not funded or endorsed by UCSB.
